speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if you have had any recent head trauma, neck stiffness, or changes in your vision? Also, have you noticed any sensitivity to light or sound?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your use of haloperidol, I need to rule out Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, so please tell me if you have experienced any muscle rigidity, tremors, or excessive sweating recently. Have you also noticed any changes in your blood pressure or heart rate?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in the context of haloperidol use, I am highly suspicious of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Creatine Kinase, Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Thyroid Stimulating Hormone, Urine Toxicology Screen.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated creatine kinase and leukocytosis strongly support Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, but we must rule out infection as a trigger. Do you have any urinary symptoms, cough, or skin lesions, and when was your last haloperidol dose?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of tics, currently on a low dose of haloperidol. Social history: Patient details on social and occupational history not provided.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of fever, altered mentation, "lead-pipe" rigidity, diaphoresis, and significantly elevated creatine kinase in a patient on haloperidol is classic for Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I do not need further questions to confirm this diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
